description.value: A prospective longitudinal study examined cortical thickness before and after adolescent initiation of alcohol and marijuana use.

spans.text: This study looked at cortical thickness estimates pre-initiation (~ age 13) and post-initiation (~ age 19) of alcohol and marijuana use in N = 69 adolescents over six years of follow-up.

value: those individuals who initiated heavy marijuana and alcohol use during adolescence would show thicker cortices over time compared to our control teens by young adulthood in frontal and temporal brain regions, likely a result of interference with typical neuromaturational processes

spans.text: We hypothesized, based on previous investigations ( ) that those individuals who initiated heavy marijuana and alcohol use during adolescence would show thicker cortices over time compared to our control teens by young adulthood in frontal and temporal brain regions, likely a result of interference with typical neuromaturational processes.

description.value: Prospective longitudinal observational cohort study with baseline and follow-up assessments.

value: Significant Group by Time effects predicted cortical thickness in 18 widespread cortical regions, bilaterally.
A more substantial decrease in cortical thickness was typically observed over time in the ALC and CON groups, while the ALC + MJ group showed less substantial thinning.
Between-group differences were generally observed at baseline, with ALC and CON demonstrating thicker cortices than ALC + MJ, but these differences were largely absent at follow-up.
